fields.name: contact_name
fields.instructions: First and last name of the contact person for the dataset. Typically this is the principal investigator of the study.

fields.name: contact_email
fields.instructions: Email address of the contact person.

fields.name: contact_institute
fields.instructions: Name of institution under which the contact person is employed.

fields.name: title
fields.instructions: A concise title for the dataset. This typically includes the dataset type, the organism studied, and conditions examined. Limit to 255 characters.
fields.example: RNA-seq analysis of neonatal mouse cochlear hair cells

fields.name: summary
fields.instructions: An abstract describing the goal of the project and the experiments that were performed.
fields.example: This study examined transcripts that are enriched in neonatal mouse cochlear hair cells. Hair cells were purified by FACS sorting for GFP fluorescence from the cochleas of transgenic mice in which the endogenous Atoh1 gene was fused with GFP.

fields.name: dataset_type
fields.instructions: Directs data to the correct part of gEAR. If your study has more than one type of data, submit each type as a separate dataset. If you are doing single-nucleus RNA-seq or SMART-seq, use single-cell-rnaseq. Use spatial for spatial transcriptomics, and epigenome for epigenome tracks (e.g. ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq).

fields.name: reference_annot_id
fields.instructions: Reference annotation the data were aligned to, as source:version. Supported sources are Ensembl, GenBank and RefSeq. For Ensembl give the release number; for GenBank and RefSeq give the assembly accession. Examples: Ensembl:93, RefSeq:GCF_000001635.27, GenBank:GCA_000001635.9. If your reference is not yet loaded into gEAR you can still upload, and the gEAR team will contact you about loading it.

fields.name: repository_accession
fields.instructions: Accession of the data in a public repository, with the repository as prefix: GEO (e.g. GEO:GSE168901), ArrayExpress (e.g. ArrayExpress:E-MTAB-11634), CNGB (e.g. CNGB:CNP0002521) or NeMO. Leave blank if the data have not been submitted to one of these.
fields.pattern_hint: GEO:, ArrayExpress:, CNGB: or NeMO: followed by the accession

fields.name: sample_taxid
fields.instructions: NCBI taxonomy ID of the one species the samples come from, e.g. human NCBI:txid9606, mouse NCBI:txid10090, rat NCBI:txid10116, zebrafish NCBI:txid7955. A gEAR dataset can only hold one species. If your study has samples from more than one species, split the data by species and submit each as its own dataset.
fields.pattern_hint: NCBI:txid followed by the numeric taxon ID

fields.name: pubmed_id
fields.instructions: PubMed ID of the publication describing the data, with "PMID:" prefix.
fields.pattern_hint: PMID: followed by the numeric PubMed ID

fields.name: keywords
fields.instructions: Up to 6 keywords or phrases related to the dataset that are not otherwise captured in the metadata, separated by commas.

fields.name: device
fields.instructions: Term ID from the Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI) 'device' branch for the device used to generate the primary data, e.g. Illumina NovaSeq 6000 OBI:0002630, Illumina HiSeq 2500 OBI:0002002. If you can't find the term you need, use the branch root term OBI:0000968 and the gEAR team will follow up with you.
fields.pattern_hint: OBI: followed by the 7-digit term number

fields.name: library_cons_method
fields.instructions: Name of the kit/protocol used for cDNA library construction or, if a kit is not used, a link to protocols.io or a DOI for the methods description.

fields.name: rna_extraction_method
fields.instructions: Name of the kit/protocol used for RNA extraction or, if a kit is not used, a link to protocols.io or a DOI for the methods description.
fields.example: High Pure RNA Isolation kit (Roche Diagnostics)

fields.name: microarray_hybridization_protocol
fields.instructions: Name of the kit/protocol used for microarray hybridization or, if a kit is not used, a link to protocols.io or a DOI for the methods description. Required for microarray datasets.

fields.name: assay
fields.instructions: Term ID from the OBI 'assay' branch for the technique used to generate the primary data, e.g. bulk RNA-seq assay OBI:0003090, single-cell RNA sequencing assay OBI:0002631, single-nucleus RNA sequencing assay OBI:0003109, microarray OBI:0400147. If you can't find the term you need, use the branch root term OBI:0000070 and the gEAR team will follow up with you.
fields.pattern_hint: OBI: followed by the 7-digit term number

fields.name: normalization_method
fields.instructions: Normalization method used on the data, e.g. TPM, RPM/CPM, RPKM/FPKM, SCnorm, GeTMM, DESeq2, ComBat-Seq, QN.

fields.name: log_transformation
fields.instructions: Transformation applied to the count data.

fields.name: primary_analysis_completed
fields.instructions: A primary analysis is the clustering and dimensionality reduction (UMAP, tSNE or PCA) run on the data before uploading, for example in Seurat or Scanpy. Choose Yes if the observation (sample) metadata includes its cluster assignments or coordinates; gEAR then checks that it can find them. Otherwise No.
